nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a finite set of vertices and let $P$ be a property of finite sets of vertices. If $t$ satisfies $P$, then there is exactly one finite set $e$ of vertices with $e \in \{t\}$ and $P(e)$.
nodes.title: Unique element of a singleton family

nodes.summary: Every finite set of vertices is independent in the empty hypergraph, the hypergraph with no edges.
nodes.title: Every set is independent in the empty hypergraph

nodes.summary: For a finite hypergraph $H$, the empty set is independent in $H$ if and only if every edge of $H$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: When the empty set is independent

nodes.summary: A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ if and only if no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Independence unfolded

nodes.summary: If a finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ and $J \subseteq I$, then $J$ is independent in $H$.
nodes.title: Subsets of independent sets are independent

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite hypergraph, that is a finite family of finite sets of vertices, called its edges. A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in $H$ when no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Independent set in a hypergraph

nodes.summary: A finite hypergraph $H$ on a vertex type $V$, that is a finite family of finite subsets of $V$, is a Steiner triple system when it is $3$-uniform (every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements) and any two distinct vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ lie together in exactly one edge of $H$.
nodes.title: Steiner triple system

nodes.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system on a vertex type $V$, then for all vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ there is exactly one edge $e$ of $H$ with $u \in e$ and $v \in e$.
nodes.title: Pairs in a Steiner triple system

nodes.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system, then $H$ is $3$-uniform: every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements.
nodes.title: Steiner triple systems are 3-uniform

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
